title: Proof-of-Concept Ops Roadmap & Staffing Kickoff — Mosaic Health POC
next_steps: Jordan to share POC runbook and sample benchmark scripts by 2026-01-10
Mosaic to provide sample dataset (anonymized) and API access by 2026-01-15
Samantha to provision preliminary Dedicated perf tests and share baseline numbers by 2026-01-20
action_items: Jordan — send runbook and benchmark scripts — 2026-01-10
Mosaic (Priya) — confirm data export and anonymization plan — 2026-01-15
Samantha — run initial latency/cost baselines on equivalent VM and share results — 2026-01-20
summary: Kickoff to align PoC success criteria, dataset and access plan, sizing assumptions, benchmark targets (p50 latency < 200ms for 512 tokens, throughput of 30 req/s steady), timeline with milestones: access setup, mid-point review, exec readout. Key risks: data anonymization, SSO/SAML, network egress policy. Agreed next steps and owners.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Samantha and Ravi from our solutions team. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha Rahman: Good thanks, we got Carlos and Priya on too. Busy week but excited to get this POC moving.
[00:15] Jordan Blake: Awesome. Goal for today is to scope the POC timeline, align on success criteria, and make sure access and data flow are clear. We'll also talk about benchmarks and who owns what. Sound good?
[00:24] Carlos Mendes: Yup. We're running a retrieval-augmented generation workflow, about 10k daily active users hitting the service during peak. Typical prompt 200–600 tokens, some longer sessions. Main concern is latency and cost.
[00:36] Samantha Chu: Great detail, Carlos. Can you clarify percentiles you'd like to optimize for? p50 vs p95?
[00:41] Carlos Mendes: p95 is what our UX team obsesses over. If p95 is > 800ms we get support tickets. Ideally p95 under 600, p50 under 200.
[00:51] Jordan Blake: Good call. For the POC we usually aim to hit target p95 within a tolerated band — we'll propose p95 < 600ms for 512 token responses, and cost per 1k tokens under a threshold.
[01:04] Priya Singh: From security side we need SOC2 type II evidence, SAML SSO for the console, and network egress controls — our legal wants a data retention clause.
[01:12] Jordan Blake: Noted. We'll share our compliance pack and SSO integration guide. For the POC we can operate inside a dedicated VPC peering or Redwood Private — whichever you prefer.
[01:22] Aisha Rahman: Peering would be easiest given our internal policies. We need to confirm whether the Dedicated option can be used for the POC; budget team is sensitive.
[01:30] Samantha Chu: We can run a Dedicated-equivalent sandbox for the POC that mirrors perf characteristics; it's called a 'dedicated trial pool' — I'll outline the cost delta in the runbook.
[01:38] Carlos Mendes: Ok. About dataset: we'll provide a 15k sample of anonymized user prompts and the retrieval index. That should be enough for benchmarking.
[01:47] Jordan Blake: Perfect. That gives us realistic request shapes. For workload sizing: what concurrency do you expect at peak?
[01:53] Carlos Mendes: Roughly 30 concurrent requests sustained for 2–3 minutes during spikes. Average qps about 8–10.
[02:02] Samantha Chu: So we should size for 30 req/s sustained with bursts to 50 for short windows. We'll run two benchmark sweeps: latency-focused (small batch sizes, low latency SLO) and throughput-focused (batching/quantization).
[02:14] Jordan Blake: Benchmarks we'll run: p50/p95 latency for 128/512 tokens, tokens/sec throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and tail latency distribution. We'll also measure cold-start/kv-cache warmup behavior.
[02:27] Priya Singh: Also log retention and audit trails — we need proof of request-level logging for two weeks.
[02:33] Jordan Blake: Yes we can enable request traces and provide audit logs for the POC window.
[02:37] Ravi Patel: Quick note: for KV cache and long conversations we saw degradation if cache isn't warmed, so test vectors should include multi-turn context to simulate realistic sessions.
[02:46] Carlos Mendes: We'll include 20% multi-turn sessions with 5–8 messages each.
[02:51] Jordan Blake: Great. Now timeline: propose kickoff this week, access and data exchange by Jan 15, initial baseline benchmarks by Jan 20, mid-point review ~ Feb 12, final exec readout week of Mar 2. Does that align?
[03:05] Aisha Rahman: That fits our roadmap. Exec readout needs to include cost savings estimate and runbook for production roll.
[03:12] Samantha Chu: We'll prepare an exec slide pack showing perf numbers, cost per 1k tokens, and recommended config (batching, quantization profile).
[03:19] Jordan Blake: Staffing — who owns the POC on your side?
[03:22] Aisha Rahman: Carlos will be technical lead, Priya owns security, and I'll be sponsor.
[03:28] Jordan Blake: On ours Jordan (me) AE, Samantha SE, Ravi deep-dive support. We'll set regular weekly 30-minute syncs and run a mid-point deep-dive.
[03:37] Priya Singh: About legal — can you send the standard DPA? We also need a short form MSA for the pilot.
[03:43] Jordan Blake: Yes, legal will send the DPA and pilot MSA today.
[03:46] Carlos Mendes: One risk — our infra team restricts outbound traffic to specific IP ranges. How do we handle that?
[03:51] Samantha Chu: We support VPC peering and static egress ranges for Dedicated — we can provide the CIDR/IPs for firewall allowlist.
[03:59] Priya Singh: Also need to confirm key management — can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS for payload encryption?
[04:06] Ravi Patel: For Private deployments yes; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and customer-managed keys for Private. We'll include options in the runbook.
[04:14] Jordan Blake: OK, let's capture next steps — I'll summarize.
[04:17] [Break — cross talk while notes are shared] 
[04:31] Jordan Blake: Recap: runbook + benchmark scripts by 2026-01-10, Mosaic to provide anonymized dataset and firewall allowlist by 2026-01-15, Samantha to run baseline perf by 2026-01-20, mid-point review 2026-02-12, exec readout week of 2026-03-02.
[04:47] Aisha Rahman: Sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood?
[04:50] Samantha Chu: Need the dataset and network details. Also legal sign-off for DPA/MSA but that usually moves quickly for pilots.
[04:58] Carlos Mendes: Alright we'll get the artifacts to you. Thanks all.
[05:02] Jordan Blake: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for weekly sync and mid-point.
[05:07] [Meeting ends]
